intended_object: The defining Hopf ideal, in the coordinate Hopf algebra k[GL₂₄], of the closed subgroup of GL₂₄ over a commutative ring k generated by the eight numbered root subgroups (positive and negative simple roots) and the rank-four weight torus of the tripled type-D₄ representation. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which cites Milne, Prop. 2.37.
explanation:
The body is `commonKernelHopfIdeal (generatorCoordinateMap k)`. That is the supremum, in the lattice of Hopf ideals, of all Hopf ideals contained in the kernel of every generator's coordinate map, so it is the largest Hopf ideal they all kill. The generator family, indexed by `(Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4) ⊕ Unit`, consists of the eight base-changed root-subgroup coordinate maps and the weight-torus coordinate map.

Under the duality between closed subgroup schemes and Hopf ideals, the largest Hopf ideal killed by all the generator maps corresponds to the smallest closed subgroup through which every generator homomorphism factors. That is the standard definition of the closed subgroup generated by a family of homomorphisms (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Prop. 2.37). Taking the supremum among Hopf ideals avoids the problem that a plain intersection of kernels need not be a Hopf ideal, which is the right choice.

The object is a specific group: a particular D₄ representation in GL₂₄. It is already stated over an arbitrary commutative ring k, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart.
